name: Chapter 7 - The AD-AS model - Comprehensive MCQ Bank

questions.text: The growth trend of an economy refers to:

options.a: only quarter-to-quarter deviations from potential output
options.b: the unemployment rate at one date
options.d: the long-run evolution of economic activity

questions.text: Business-cycle fluctuations are:

options.b: deviations of actual GDP around its longer-run/potential path
options.d: only changes in the CPI basket

questions.text: The output gap is defined in the slides as:
A positive output gap means:

options.a: unemployment is necessarily above its natural rate
options.c: actual output Y is above potential output Yn

questions.text: A negative output gap means:

options.a: actual output is below potential output
options.b: the economy is necessarily in long-run growth
options.d: actual output is above potential output

questions.text: An economic expansion can be defined in several ways in the slides, including a phase in which:

options.a: real GDP growth is positive or above trend, or the level is above trend depending on the convention used
options.b: real GDP must fall for two consecutive quarters
options.c: the output gap must always be exactly zero

questions.text: An economic downturn is described as a phase in which:

options.a: GDP necessarily falls by more than 10%

questions.text: A recession is a phase in which:

options.a: real GDP decreases, with some definitions requiring two consecutive quarters of decline
options.c: GDP growth merely slows but remains positive by definition
options.d: GDP falls by at least 10% by definition

questions.text: A depression is used for:

options.a: a particularly severe recession, with the slides using a roughly 10% GDP decline threshold
options.d: any single quarter with slower growth

questions.text: A trough is:

options.c: the highest point of an expansion
options.d: the lowest level of economic activity reached during a recession phase

questions.text: A peak is:

options.b: the lowest point of a recession
options.c: the highest point of activity reached during an expansion
options.d: a permanent rise in potential GDP

options.a: always move in the opposite direction from GDP
options.d: tend to move in the same direction as GDP

questions.text: Which variable is cited as particularly volatile over the business cycle?

options.a: the natural unemployment rate by construction
options.b: the working-age population over one quarter
options.d: the nominal value of currency by definition

questions.text: House sales are cited as:
The AD-AS model is designed mainly for:

options.b: the very long-run growth trend only

questions.text: Compared with IS-LM, AD-AS adds explicitly:

options.a: supply-side adjustment through wages and prices
options.c: a permanent assumption of fixed prices

questions.text: IS-LM can be viewed as overlooking the supply side because it assumes:

options.b: the labour market is always at u_n
options.c: underutilised capacity and fixed wages/prices so firms meet demand at unchanged P

questions.text: Why is the AS curve upward sloping?

options.a: Higher Y shifts money demand left.
options.b: Higher Y lowers expected prices by identity.
options.c: Higher Y raises employment, lowers unemployment, strengthens wage claims and leads firms to set higher prices.
options.d: Higher Y raises unemployment and lowers wages.

questions.text: For a given expected price level, the AS curve passes through (Yn,P^e) because at Yn:

options.a: the labour market is at its natural equilibrium and P=P^e

questions.text: An increase in expected price level P^e shifts AS:

options.c: right with no change in prices

questions.text: The mechanism behind an upward AS shift after higher P^e is:

options.b: higher expected prices → higher nominal wage claims → higher prices set by firms
options.c: higher expected prices → lower employment automatically
options.d: higher expected prices → lower wages → lower P

questions.text: The aggregate-demand curve is derived from:

options.a: the IS-LM equilibrium as the price level P varies

A rise in real money balances shifts LM:

options.a: down/right and tends to increase equilibrium output

The chapter also notes a possible purchasing-power channel from P to IS when:

options.b: all nominal contracts are perfectly indexed

options.d: the economy is closed by definition

questions.text: In an open-economy competition channel, a rise in domestic P at unchanged foreign prices tends to:

options.c: leave net exports unchanged by definition
options.d: make exports less competitive and imports relatively more attractive, reducing net exports

questions.text: For simplified graphical analysis, the course mainly attributes the slope of AD to:

options.a: a direct effect of P on potential output
options.d: the effect of P on real money supply and therefore LM

questions.text: Short-run AD-AS equilibrium is located at:

options.b: the intersection of WS and PS only
options.c: the intersection of AD and AS for the current expected price level

questions.text: If short-run equilibrium has Y ≠ Yn, then:

options.a: the labour market is away from its medium-run equilibrium and wage/price expectations adjust over time
options.b: the economy is already in stable medium-run equilibrium

questions.text: Medium-run AD-AS equilibrium requires:
With adaptive price-level expectations P^e_{t+1}=P_t, if a positive demand shock creates Y_t>Yn and P_t>P^e_t, then next period:

options.a: expected prices fall and AS shifts downward
options.b: AD shifts left by expectation alone
options.d: expected prices rise and AS shifts upward

questions.text: As AS shifts upward following a positive output gap, the model predicts:

options.b: the money supply rises by identity
options.c: P rises further while Y moves back toward Yn
options.d: P falls while Y moves farther above Yn

The short-run effect of restrictive fiscal policy in AD-AS is:

In the medium run after a permanent reduction in G, output:

options.c: returns to Yn while the price level is lower

questions.text: Opening the IS-LM "black box", the initial fall in G shifts IS:

options.c: left, reducing Y and r if P were fixed

questions.text: As P falls after the fiscal contraction, real money balances rise, so LM:
In the medium run after fiscal consolidation, with Yn and taxes held fixed, lower G must be offset in the goods-market identity by:

options.b: higher private C and I, associated with a lower interest rate

questions.text: An expansive monetary policy shifts AD:
In the short run after an increase in M^s, the model predicts:

options.a: higher Y, higher P and a lower interest rate relative to the initial equilibrium
options.b: lower Y, lower P and higher r

questions.text: As prices rise following monetary expansion, real money balances:

options.b: become equal to nominal money supply
options.d: fall relative to what they would be at the initial price, partially reversing the LM shift

questions.text: In the medium run after a purely procyclical permanent monetary expansion:

options.c: Y and r return to initial real levels while P rises proportionally with M^s
options.d: P returns to its initial level

questions.text: Money neutrality in this chapter means that in the medium run:

options.b: a procyclical change in money supply affects nominal variables but not real Y and r
options.d: money has no short-run effect either

questions.text: Why is monetary policy still useful despite medium-run money neutrality?

options.a: It permanently raises potential output regardless of technology.
options.b: Countercyclical monetary policy can speed the return of Y toward Yn and limit overheating or deep slumps.
options.d: It eliminates the natural unemployment rate.

questions.text: A decrease in competition intensity corresponds in the model to:
A higher markup θ shifts the PS curve:

options.a: down in real-wage space and raises natural unemployment

questions.text: A higher natural unemployment rate implies potential output Yn:
A negative supply shock that raises θ therefore shifts AS:

options.b: up/left relative to the old natural-output point

questions.text: A negative supply shock can generate stagflation because in the short run it tends to:

options.d: raise both output and employment permanently

questions.text: In the medium run after a permanent negative supply shock, the economy converges to:

options.a: the old Yn with the old price level
options.c: a lower Yn with a higher price level than before, given unchanged AD fundamentals

questions.text: Economists can disagree over policy partly because they may disagree about:

options.a: how quickly the economy converges from short-run disequilibrium to medium-run equilibrium
options.c: whether GDP is a flow variable

questions.text: Economists may also disagree about:

options.b: the size and sign of the current output gap
options.c: the definition of a price index baseline

questions.text: German reunification in 1990 is presented as initially involving:

options.a: a large fiscal expansion associated with East German catching-up and public investment
options.d: a monetary expansion with no fiscal change

questions.text: The Bundesbank responded to reunification-related inflationary pressure with:
The combination of fiscal expansion and monetary contraction caused:

options.a: a sharp fall in interest rates
options.c: a very sharp rise in interest rates that restrained German activity
options.d: a permanent rise in potential GDP

questions.text: The restrictive German monetary policy affected the rest of Europe because:

options.a: the CPI forced rates to be equal
options.b: all European countries shared a single currency already in 1990
options.c: countries seeking to maintain fixed currency parities had to align their monetary policies with Germany

questions.text: The episode is described as an example of:

options.a: money neutrality with no short-run effects

questions.text: A permanent reduction in G followed by full medium-run adjustment changes the composition of demand even though Y returns to Yn. The course predicts:

options.c: G lower and C/I lower with Y unchanged by contradiction
